claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified because aggregate performance clears the deployment bar and the small-business support weakness can be handled through explicit model-card disclosure, while the unapproved monitoring proposal is not relied upon as a mitigation.
specific_concerns: Only the actor's summary is available; the cited evidence is not directly inspectable in this role.
The policy path is plausible only if the small-business support weakness is in fact disclosed and disclosure is sufficient for this specific weakness.
The packet asserts quantitative results and uncertainty claims without underlying tables, thresholds, confidence intervals, or sample counts.

The unresolved materiality predicate remains thinly supported: the summary says the weakness is 'material' enough to disclose, but does not show why disclosure alone is sufficient rather than further mitigation or deferral.
unsupported_claims: The model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by 2.2 percentage points.
The small-business support slice is below both its warning threshold and its preferred threshold.
The slice has a smaller sample and wider confidence interval that justify rechecking in the next batch.
The draft monitoring mitigation is unapproved.
Disclosure, rather than approved mitigation, is sufficient for certification in this case.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying evaluation results for aggregate and small-business support slice performance, including exact thresholds and observed values.
Provide sample sizes and confidence intervals for the cited subgroup and aggregate metrics.
Provide the actual model-card disclosure text or draft showing the weakness is explicitly disclosed.
Provide the approval status record for the proposed post-launch monitoring mitigation.
Provide any policy interpretation or precedent showing that this type of disclosed subgroup weakness may still be certified without approved mitigation.
decision_criteria: Certification is allowed only if a material weakness is disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates may support launch readiness but do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty may reduce confidence but does not resolve an otherwise unresolved materiality question.
An evidentially supported compliant finding requires more than the actor's summary when quantitative and approval-dependent predicates are central to the conclusion.
